images.title: Count the zeroes, then hop
images.purpose: Recap the method: count the zeroes in the divisor, hop the point left that many places, and fill empty places with zeroes.
images.composition: One large worked example in the centre with three hop arrows over the number, the result below it, and a small two fact unit strip along the bottom.
exact_structure: Centre top: the divisor 1000 written large with its 3 zeroes in reddish purple #CC79A7 and the 1 in dark text; under it the note 3 zeroes.

Centre: the number 45.2 in teal #0072B2 digits, with one small grey #6B7280 added 0 written just in front of the 4 (so the row reads 0 4 5 . 2); 3 reddish purple #CC79A7 curved arrows above it show the point hopping left over 5, then 4, then the added 0; under the arrows the note 3 places left.
Below: the result line 45.2 ÷ 1000 = 0.0452, with the result 0.0452 in green #009E73.
Bottom strip, small and grey #6B7280 outlined: two boxes reading 1 m = 100 cm and 1 cm = 10 mm.
rejection: more or fewer than 3 hop arrows
the point hopping right instead of left
images.takeaway: Count the zeroes in the divisor and move the point that many places left, writing zeroes where places run out.
images.description: The divisor 1000 with its three zeroes in purple, three arrows hopping the point of 45.2 to the left, the result 45.2 ÷ 1000 = 0.0452, and two unit facts below.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept on dividing by 10, 100 and 1000 and converting lengths.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to say the three steps aloud while tracing the arrows: count, hop, fill with zeroes.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap of the count and hop method supports the practice questions.
